findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. PIC said that they will get the training done. The other person with a manager certification was out. Ensure that there is at least one CFPM present at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following were observed during today’s inspection,
1. The sanitizer concentration in the dish machine was measured at 0ppm. PIC told inspector that they will use the three compartment sink until the dish machine is fixed.
2. The chlorine sanitizer in the sani bucket in the kitchen was observed to be unreadable. PIC was made aware and a new sani bucket was made. (COS) 
 Ensure that the sanitizer concentration in the sanitizer buckets and dish machine is continuously checked at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the plumbing line supplying the dish machine to be in disrepair. There was a rush of water leak observed while the dish machine cycle ran. PIC told inspector that they were going to call the EcoLab technician to get the issue fix. Ensure that the relevant repairs is done to be in compliance with the LAW.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an opening ceiling tile above the fryers including the kitchen. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the ceiling tile is replaced sealing the opening.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: The hood ventilation was observed to have an accumulation of soil and grease buildup dangling. PIC was made aware. PIC called the company hired for the routine cleaning and the hood service was scheduled while inspector was present. Ensure that the hood systems is routinely cleaned to avoid the accumulation of grease and soil.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Facility was observed to not be in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that they do not have certification however, will be getting the training done soon. Ensure that CFPMs receive allergen training to be in compliance with the LAW. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.comment:
The following were observed, 
1. The nozzles of the soda guns at the bar were observed with an accumulation of soil. Education was carried out. The nozzles were cleaned immediately. (COS)

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a box and several bags of single service items being stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Education as carried out. The single service items were removed to be stored properly in another location.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: A jug of milk was observed opened and not date marked in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC and PIC mentioned that the jug had been open two days prior. The date marking was then corrected. Ensure that food items are date marked properly if they are not used within 24 hours after opening to prevent listeria growth.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION. The walk-in freezer is observed to have peeling paint on the ceiling. PIC was made aware that this is a repeat from previous inspection on 10/22/2024 and PIC ensured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure the areas with the paint coming off are properly scraped and then a new sealant, such as paint, is utilized to reseal that area that was scraped. The repair in the walk-in freezer should be done in a manner that allows the repaired surfaces to be smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the bar hand washing sink was blocked with dishes and cleaning equipment. The PIC moved the items out of the hand sink during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks remain accessible at all times for employee use. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: In the single door cooler in the kitchen, there was observed raw shrimp stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) food products. These items were inverted during today’s inspection. Ensure food items are stored properly to prevent contamination during storage, preparation, and display. This is a repeat from the 03/15/2024 inspection and the facility will be receiving a repeat letter to document the violation. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed both kitchen sanitizer buckets were testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. A capful of bleach was added to both during the inspection to make the sanitizer solutions 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that chemical sanitizer solutions meet the proper criteria (bleach = 100-200 ppm). Also ensure that test strips are used on a regular basis to test the sanitizer solution concentrations.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: The walk in freezer door gasket is observed to be in a state of disrepair where there are gaps present from the gasket not being sealed properly. Ensure this gasket is repaired to create a seal that is in good repair to protect the integrity of the freezer temperatures during peak hours and during heat waves. This item is a repeat violation from the 8/23/23 and 3/15/2024 original inspections and the facility will be receiving a notice to correct to document the violation. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the gasket of the single standing Pepsi cooler on the cook line is in disrepair with the gasket disconnecting from the door. Equipment must be maintained in good repair. Ensure that the gasket is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.
